core_obligations: Write I = (f_1, ..., f_r) and let K_n^bullet be the Koszul complex with respect to f_1^n, ..., f_r^n (proof lines 27227-27228).
Use the derived completion Koszul statement to reduce to the displayed chain of equalities identifying R lim(K tensor^L_A K_n^bullet) with R lim(K tensor^L_A A/I^n) (proof lines 27229-27235).

Use the sequence of Koszul complexes statement to conclude that the pro-objects {K_n^bullet} and {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} in D(A) are isomorphic, and observe that {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} and {A/I^n} are isomorphic (proof lines 27236-27239).
Conclude that the map from left to right is an isomorphism by the statement on tensor products and R lim respecting pro-isomorphisms (proof lines 27240-27241).
difficulty_reason: Let A be a Noetherian ring and I an ideal. The proposition asserts that the functor sending K in D(A) to the derived limit K' = R lim(K tensor^L_A A/I^n) is the left adjoint to the inclusion functor D_comp(A) -> D(A) constructed in the derived completion statement (source lines 27217-27224). The proof reduces the naive completion along a different presentation of the ideal to the Koszul presentation. Write I = (f_1, ..., f_r) and let K_n^bullet be the Koszul complex with respect to f_1^n, ..., f_r^n (proof lines 27227-27228). By the derived completion Koszul statement it suffices to prove the displayed three-term chain of equalities identifying R lim(K tensor^L_A K_n^bullet) with both R lim(K tensor^L_A A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)) and R lim(K tensor^L_A A/I^n) (proof lines 27229-27235). By the sequence of Koszul complexes statement the pro-objects {K_n^bullet} and {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} in D(A) are isomorphic, and the pro-objects {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} and {A/I^n} are visibly isomorphic (proof lines 27236-27239). The map from left to right is therefore an isomorphism by the statement on tensor products and R lim respecting pro-isomorphisms (proof lines 27240-27241). The non-routine content is the choice of presentation: replacing the naive system A/I^n by the Koszul system K_n^bullet puts the computation in the framework of the Koszul-derived completion statement, and the two pro-isomorphism statements then transport the adjunction.
